articles.title: Dinamarca aprova acordo militar com EUA e Groenlândia | G1
articles.standfirst: Acordo autoriza ampliação da presença militar americana na ilha, mas mantém o território autônomo sob controle da Dinamarca; Parlamento groenlandês já havia aprovado o texto.
articles.summary: Acordo autoriza ampliação da presença militar americana na ilha, mas mantém o território autônomo sob controle da Dinamarca; Parlamento groenlandês já havia aprovado o texto.
articles.body:
O ministro das Relações Exteriores da Dinamarca, Lars Løkke Rasmussen (à direita), participa da segunda etapa do processo legislativo e da votação do acordo de segurança entre Dinamarca, Groenlândia e Estados Unidos, no plenário do Parlamento, no Palácio de Christiansborg, em Copenhague. — Foto: Mads Claus Rasmussen / Associated Press

O Parlamento da Dinamarca aprovou nesta quinta-feira (19) um acordo negociado com a Groenlândia e os Estados Unidos para reforçar a segurança no Ártico e no Atlântico Norte.

A votação ocorre após meses de pressão do presidente americano, Donald Trump , para assumir o controle da Groenlândia, território semiautônomo pertencente à Dinamarca, país integrante da Organização do Tratado do Atlântico Norte (Otan)

O acordo trilateral, firmado entre Trump e os líderes dinamarqueses e groenlandeses, abre caminho para a ampliação da presença militar dos Estados Unidos na ilha e reduz as tensões provocadas pelas repetidas declarações do presidente americano sobre transformar o território em parte dos EUA.

A proposta foi aprovada por 109 votos a zero no Parlamento dinamarquês. A votação representa a última etapa para a entrada em vigor do acordo, que já havia sido aprovado sem oposição pelo Parlamento da Groenlândia no início deste mês.

O texto estabelece que o acordo entrará em vigor quando Dinamarca e Groenlândia notificarem os Estados Unidos, por meio de uma nota diplomática, de que seus respectivos parlamentos concluíram todos os procedimentos necessários.

O embaixador dos Estados Unidos na Dinamarca, Kenneth Howery, comemorou o apoio dos parlamentares dinamarqueses à ratificação do acordo. Segundo ele, a aprovação abre caminho para que o documento entre em vigor.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, a primeira-ministra da Dinamarca, Mette Frederiksen, e o primeiro-ministro da Groenlândia, Jens-Frederik Nielsen, participam de um evento trilateral de assinatura de um acordo sobre a segurança da Groenlândia. — Foto: Kylie Cooper/Reuters

"Este acordo é uma conquista extraordinária, que moderniza nossa parceria diante dos desafios de segurança do futuro e reforça a proteção dos Estados Unidos, do Reino da Dinamarca, incluindo a Groenlândia, e de toda a Otan", escreveu Howery na rede social X.

O objetivo do tratado é ampliar a presença militar americana na Groenlândia, mantendo o território autônomo sob controle dinamarquês. O acordo também continuará válido caso a ilha decida conquistar a independência no futuro.

Trump e os líderes da Dinamarca e da Groenlândia assinaram o documento em setembro, em Nova York, após meses de negociações reservadas . As conversas buscavam responder às preocupações de segurança do presidente americano e aos temores dinamarqueses e groenlandeses de uma possível anexação pelos Estados Unidos.

O acordo amplia os termos de um tratado de defesa firmado em 1951. Pelo documento, os Estados Unidos poderão expandir sua presença militar na ilha e modernizar e ampliar as atividades na Base Espacial de Pituffik, localizada no noroeste da Groenlândia.

O governo americano também poderá estabelecer áreas de defesa em Narsarsuaq, no sul, e Mestersvig, no leste do território. O tratado permite ainda a criação de outras zonas militares e o reforço das operações e instalações de defesa americanas na ilha.

articles.standfirst: Viagens atenderão o público do festival entre sexta e domingo, com retornos programados até a madrugada.
articles.summary: As linhas para o FASC 2026 saem dos terminais Zona Sul, Centro e Mercado, com reforço na frota e retornos programados entre meia-noite e 3h da manhã.
articles.body:
Interior de ônibus; catraca; Aracaju — Foto: Ronald Almeida/PMA

Três linhas especiais de ônibus em Aracaju foram criadas para atender ao público que quiser prestigiar o Festival de Artes de São Cristóvão (Fasc) 2026. As linhas sairão dos terminais Zona Sul, Centro e Mercado.

Segundo a Prefeitura de Aracaju, a iniciativa busca facilitar o deslocamento dos usuários do transporte público até o Centro Histórico de São Cristóvão.

Nesta sexta-feira (20), as partidas ocorrerão às 18h, 19h, 20h e 21h. Já no sábado (21) e no domingo (22), as saídas serão às 12h, 14h, 16h, 18h, 19h30 e 20h30. Para o retorno, as três linhas terão partidas à meia-noite, 1h, 2h e 3h, com embarque na Rua Vinte e Quatro de Outubro e destino aos respectivos terminais de origem.

Ainda de acordo com a Prefeitura, veículos extras poderão ser disponibilizados, caso haja necessidade. Além disso, foi solicitado o reforço da frota das linhas regulares 307, 311 e 312 durante os dias do festival.

A passagem das linhas especiais será cobrada normalmente, com utilização dos validadores instalados nos veículos. Os ônibus terão identificação específica no letreiro, com o nome da linha e a indicação FASC 2026, para facilitar o reconhecimento pelos passageiros.

articles.title: 'Voltem para a sala de aula', incentiva homem barrado no Enem | G1
articles.standfirst: Carlos Eduardo Pereira da Silva, de 57 anos, terá nova chance de fazer o Enem após ter sido barrado por estar de bicicleta no último domingo (15) em Campos (RJ). Ele contou que perdeu os pais, viveu em situação de rua até decidir focar nos estudos e não desistir.

articles.body:
Aos 57 anos, após perder os pais, viver em situação de rua, passar por 13 abrigos e enfrentar o alcoolismo, Carlos Eduardo Pereira da Silva transformou a própria trajetória em uma mensagem para quem abandonou os estudos.

Enquanto tenta realizar o sonho de ingressar na faculdade por meio do Enem há dez anos, ele faz um apelo para que outras pessoas não desistam de construir um futuro melhor.

"Aqueles que estão fora da sala de aula, voltem para a sala de aula. Matriculem-se, vão estudar, buscar um futuro. Vocês são inteligentes. Não percam tempo, porque a hora de vencer é agora!", disse.

A história de Carlos Eduardo ganhou repercussão depois que ele foi impedido de entrar no local de prova do Enem, em Campos dos Goytacazes (RJ), no último domingo (15), por estar de bicicleta. Segundo o Inep, ele poderá solicitar a reaplicação do exame.

Mas, para ele, o episódio é apenas mais um obstáculo em uma caminhada marcada por recomeços. Ao g1 , o estudante relembrou os desafios que enfrentou até retomar os estudos e reconstruir a vida.

Carlos Eduardo incentiva outras pessoas a voltarem a estudar, depois enfrentar o alcoolismo e viver em situação de rua em Campos — Foto: Josué Amador/g1

"Me tornei dependente da bebida alcoólica e já passei por 13 abrigos. Mas a bebida não me deixava parar em nenhum deles. Então, eu decidi me redimir, e agora estou próximo de concluir a segunda prova do Enem, que é um sonho que persigo há 10 anos. Nunca desisti. Eu sou mais que vencedor", afirmou.

Desempregado, Carlos sonha em cursar Serviço Social e vê na educação uma oportunidade de transformação. Desde junho deste ano, ele participa de um curso de cuidador social e de um preparatório para concursos públicos e para o Enem oferecidos pela Subsecretaria de Igualdade Racial e Direitos Humanos de Campos (SIRDH).

Segundo Priscila Pinheiro, chefe de Políticas de Ações Afirmativas e coordenadora dos cursos, ele recebeu gratuitamente o material didático para acompanhar as aulas. A formatura no curso de cuidador social está prevista para 10 de dezembro, quando receberá o certificado de conclusão.

Mesmo após o episódio no Enem, Carlos seguirá no preparatório e continuará sendo acompanhado até conquistar a aprovação que busca há uma década.

"Ele vai continuar com a gente até conseguir essa segunda fase. Mesmo se não passar, acredito que vai continuar com a gente, porque já virou da família", afirmou Priscila.

No domingo (15), Carlos chegou à Universidade Estácio de Sá quando faltava apenas um minuto para o fechamento dos portões. Ao tentar entrar com a bicicleta, teve o acesso impedido por agentes de segurança, que alegaram a proibição de entrada com veículo.

A situação foi registrada por pessoas que acompanhavam a cena e se solidarizaram com o candidato.

"O portão estava aberto. Estava aberto. Eu seguro a bicicleta. Isso é um absurdo", disseram testemunhas aos seguranças.

Em nota, o Instituto Nacional de Estudos e Pesquisas Educacionais Anísio Teixeira (Inep) informou que notificou a empresa aplicadora sobre o caso e garantiu que o participante poderá solicitar a reaplicação da prova.

Para Carlos, no entanto, a principal mensagem da história vai além do episódio vivido no Enem. Depois de superar o alcoolismo, a situação de rua e a passagem por 13 abrigos, ele quer mostrar que sempre é possível recomeçar por meio da educação.

articles.title: IPVA 2027 no ES: pagamento começa em abril e pode ser parcelado | G1
articles.standfirst: Pagamentos poderão ser feitos à vista, com desconto de 15%, ou em seis parcelas. As datas do início variam entre 1º e 8 de abril, de acordo com o número final da placa.
articles.summary: Pagamentos poderão ser feitos à vista, com desconto de 15%, ou em seis parcelas. As datas do início variam entre 1º e 8 de abril, de acordo com o número final da placa.
articles.body:
Projeto propõe antecipar IPVA 2027 para dezembro e dar desconto de 15% — Foto: Detran/Reprodução

Atenção, motoristas! O pagamento do Imposto sobre Propriedade de Veículos Automotores (IPVA) de 2027 no Espírito Santo vai começar no primeiro dia do mês de abril. Os condutores podem optar por pagar a conta à vista, com desconto de 15%, ou parcelar em seis vezes.

As datas do início variam entre 1º e 8 de abril, de acordo com o final da placa do veículo. Para quem optar pelo parcelamento, as cotas vencem de abril a setembro. O calendário foi definido pelo decreto nº 6530-R/2026, publicado nesta quarta-feira (18). Confira a tabela abaixo:

Vencimentos do IPVA de 2027 (todos os veículos)

No Espírito Santo, a alíquota do IPVA é a menor da Região Sudeste e uma das menores do Brasil: 1% para motos, ônibus e caminhões; e 2% para carros de passeio e utilitários.

Em 2027, veículos fabricados até 2011 estarão isentos do pagamento do imposto, conforme a legislação estadual, que concede o benefício aos veículos com mais de 15 anos de fabricação. A isenção é automática, sem necessidade de solicitação pelo proprietário.

Os boletos do IPVA 2027 estarão disponíveis a partir de janeiro nos sites da Sefaz e do Detran|ES . Os órgãos alertam que não enviam cobranças por Correios, e-mail, SMS ou aplicativos de mensagens.

Para evitar golpes, o contribuinte deve emitir o Documento Único de Arrecadação (DUA) diretamente nos sites oficiais, sem clicar em links recebidos. O pagamento poderá ser feito por código de barras ou Pix, além de terminais bancários e casas lotéricas.

No Pix, é necessário conferir se o destinatário é o Departamento Estadual de Trânsito do Espírito Santo, CNPJ 28.162.105/0001-66. A Sefaz recomenda que o contribuinte imprima e arquive o DUA pago para eventuais conferências.

articles.title: O que pesa na decisão de empreender para as mulheres do Amazonas? | G1
articles.standfirst: No Amazonas, um levantamento do Sebrae referente ao quarto trimestre de 2024 identificou cerca de 175 mil mulheres donas de negócios, ou 27,9% do total estadual.
articles.summary: No Amazonas, um levantamento do Sebrae referente ao quarto trimestre de 2024 identificou cerca de 175 mil mulheres donas de negócios, ou 27,9% do total estadual.
articles.body:
Empreendedorismo femininp em Manaus. — Foto: Divulgação

Antes de aceitar uma encomenda maior, uma mulher que trabalha por conta própria precisa fazer algumas contas. Quanto custa comprar o material antes de receber pelo serviço? Quem ficará com as crianças se a entrega exigir mais horas de trabalho? Será possível pagar alguém para ajudar? No dia 19 de novembro, Dia Mundial do Empreendedorismo Feminino, essas perguntas merecem espaço no debate sobre negócios. Elas fazem parte das condições em que uma empresa nasce e das possibilidades que terá para crescer.

O Brasil encerrou 2025 com 10,4 milhões de mulheres donas de negócios, segundo estudo do Serviço Brasileiro de Apoio às Micro e Pequenas Empresas (Sebrae), com base na Pesquisa Nacional por Amostra de Domicílios Contínua (PNAD Contínua), do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE). Elas representavam 34,3% dos donos de negócios do país. Em dez anos, o número de empreendedoras cresceu 27%.

No Amazonas, um levantamento do Sebrae referente ao quarto trimestre de 2024 identificou cerca de 175 mil mulheres donas de negócios, ou 27,9% do total estadual. Entre elas, 78,1% eram negras. O estudo reúne empregadoras e trabalhadoras por conta própria, situações que podem ser muito diferentes em renda, estrutura e capacidade de contratar. Uma mulher que vende alimentos para sustentar a casa e outra que administra uma empresa com funcionários aparecem nesse universo, embora tenham necessidades distintas.

O avanço da escolaridade trouxe uma informação importante para essa discussão. Segundo o Sebrae, no fim de 2025, a proporção de mulheres donas de negócios com ensino superior incompleto ou mais superava a dos homens em 13 pontos percentuais. Ainda assim, o rendimento médio delas era cerca de 24% inferior. As empreendedoras recebiam, em média, R$ 2.929,94, ante R$ 3.864,12 dos homens.

Para quem interrompeu os estudos ao assumir os cuidados da família, voltar à sala de aula pode exigir dinheiro, transporte e alguém com quem dividir essas responsabilidades. Para quem conseguiu estudar, o dado nacional mostra que a formação convive com uma diferença persistente de renda. É preciso olhar também para o setor em que a mulher atua, as horas que consegue dedicar ao trabalho e as condições de acesso a clientes e financiamento.

O tempo disponível é parte dessa conta. Na região Norte, em 2022, as mulheres dedicavam, em média, 20,3 horas semanais aos afazeres domésticos e ao cuidado de pessoas. Entre os homens, eram 11,5 horas, segundo o IBGE. A diferença de quase nove horas por semana pode representar um curso que fica para depois, uma visita comercial desmarcada ou menos tempo para organizar as finanças do negócio. Esse trabalho, muitas vezes pouco reconhecido (e até invisível) consome horas e energia. Quando a responsabilidade pelo cuidado recai sempre sobre a mesma pessoa, suas escolhas profissionais ficam mais estreitas.

No Polo Industrial de Manaus (PIM), as mulheres ocupavam 35.637 dos 129.278 postos informados pelas empresas à Superintendência da Zona Franca de Manaus (Suframa) em abril de 2026. Eram 27,57% da mão de obra efetiva, temporária e terceirizada registrada naquele mês. Esse retrato merece ser acompanhado junto às oportunidades de formação técnica e de progressão na carreira. Para compreender por que uma mulher decide empreender, é importante conhecer também as alternativas de emprego que ela encontra.

Uma vaga com renda previsível pode permitir que ela poupe e experimente um negócio aos poucos. Em outras circunstâncias, trabalhar por conta própria é o caminho disponível para manter a renda e conciliar os horários da família. A flexibilidade, porém, pode vir acompanhada de jornadas que avançam pela noite e da dificuldade de separar o dinheiro da casa do dinheiro necessário à atividade.

No crédito, o Sebrae identifica obstáculos como juros elevados, exigência de garantias, histórico financeiro limitado e burocracia. Há instrumentos para enfrentar parte dessas barreiras. Em 2025, empreendedoras acessaram R$ 734 milhões em financiamentos com garantia do Fampe Mulher, iniciativa do Fundo de Aval às Micro e Pequenas Empresas. O aval pode viabilizar uma operação que seria recusada por falta de garantia. Para a mulher que toma o empréstimo, continua sendo decisivo saber se a parcela cabe na renda do negócio.

Quando o dinheiro do negócio também sustenta a casa

A paraense Samila Pinheiro começou a vender dindins em 2014, quando estava desempregada e precisava sustentar o filho pequeno. Uma polpa de cupuaçu que encontrou no freezer deu origem ao Dindin da Mila. Conseguir clientes foi uma parte do caminho. Aprender a administrar o dinheiro exigiu outras tentativas. Segundo seu relato, ela quebrou oito vezes, apesar de vender bem, porque usava o dinheiro das vendas para cobrir as despesas de casa.

A receita da venda tem de pagar a alimentação, mas também precisa financiar os ingredientes da próxima produção. Sem essa separação, até um produto com boa procura pode ficar sem dinheiro para continuar sendo feito. Samila conta que aprendeu a gerenciar o negócio com o apoio do Instituto Consulado da Mulher, em 2018. Mais tarde, passou a ensinar receitas e gestão a outras mulheres. Sua trajetória mostra o que orientação e apoio podem representar para quem precisa viver do próprio trabalho.

Poder decidir sobre o próprio dinheiro pode fortalecer a autoconfiança e ampliar a liberdade de escolha. Essa autonomia é especialmente difícil de conquistar quando há controle financeiro dentro de uma relação. Na Pesquisa Nacional de Violência contra a Mulher de 2025, do DataSenado, 27% das brasileiras com 16 anos ou mais declararam já ter sofrido violência doméstica ou familiar provocada por homem ao longo da vida. A renda própria pode ampliar as possibilidades de escolha, acompanhada de proteção e de uma rede de apoio.

Diante desse panorama que lancei hoje, 19 de novembro, o livro Amazônidas – Retratos e Trajetórias de Mulheres que Empreendem, patrocinado pelo Instituto de Desenvolvimento Tecnológico (INDT), com 70 histórias dos nove estados da Amazônia Legal. Ao reunir esses relatos, quis registrar como cada mulher construiu seu trabalho e quais circunstâncias influenciaram suas decisões. Há experiências de negócios, de retomada dos estudos, de recomeços e de coletivos de mulheres.

A obra não se propõe a ser um manifesto feminista. Acredito na parceria entre homens e mulheres, na divisão das responsabilidades e nas oportunidades de cada pessoa desenvolver suas capacidades. Foi com esse olhar que procurei ouvir e registrar as experiências dessas mulheres.

Manter uma atividade exige administrar custos, conseguir clientes e lidar com a incerteza da renda. A tarefa se torna mais difícil para quem acumula o cuidado da família e enfrenta preconceitos ou restrições à própria autonomia. Registrar essas trajetórias é ampliar o alcance da voz dessas mulheres e compartilhar experiências que podem orientar outras em suas escolhas e encorajá-las a ocupar novos espaços.

Neste dia, celebrar as conquistas também pede uma reflexão sobre como dividir melhor as responsabilidades e ampliar as oportunidades. Nossas mulheres da Amazônia produzem, pesquisam, educam, criam negócios e sustentam famílias. Que encontrem apoio para continuar estudando, decidir sobre a própria renda e fazer crescer os projetos aos quais dedicam tanto de suas vidas!

Cristina Monte é jornalista, colunista e analista de negócios, com atuação na cobertura de indústria, inovação e desenvolvimento econômico na Amazônia.

articles.title: Feriadão no ES terá temperaturas elevadas, chuva e risco de granizo | G1
articles.standfirst: Alerta laranja do Inmet prevê ventos de até 100 km/h na sexta-feira (20). No sábado (21) e domingo (22), o aviso passa a amarelo, com ventos de até 60 km/h.
articles.summary: Alerta laranja do Inmet prevê ventos de até 100 km/h na sexta-feira (20). No sábado (21) e domingo (22), o aviso passa a amarelo, com ventos de até 60 km/h.
articles.body:
Tempo fechado em Vitória — Foto: GloboNews/Reprodução

O feriado de Consciência Negra no Espírito Santo será de tempo instável, com momentos de sol e chuva. O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu um alerta laranja de tempestade para esta sexta-feira (20), com previsão de até 100 mm de chuva por dia, ventos de até 100 km/h e possibilidade de granizo.

Já para sábado (21) e domingo (22), os avisos são amarelos, com previsão de até 50 mm de chuva por dia e ventos de até 60 km/h.

Ou seja: o calor deve predominar durante o dia, enquanto que à tarde, o tempo pode fechar, formar nuvens pesadas e chover.

De acordo com o Instituto Capixaba de Pesquisa, Assistência Técnica e Extensão Rural (Incaper), a previsão é de sol entre nuvens e chuvas rápidas e isoladas em todas as regiões na sexta (20) e no sábado (21), principalmente à tarde.

Já no domingo (22), o tempo começa com mais nebulosidade, mas o sol aparece ao longo do dia. Há previsão de pancadas de chuva na Região Sul à tarde, e na Grande Vitória e na Região Serrana, à noite.

Sexta (20/11) - Feriado de Dia da Consciência Negra

O tempo fica instável e abafado em todo o Espírito Santo. O dia começa com sol, mas a nebulosidade aumenta à tarde, com previsão de chuva rápida e isolada em todas as regiões, exceto no Norte, onde não há previsão de chuva.

O sábado começa com céu nublado em todo território capixaba, mas terá períodos de abertura de sol ao longo do dia. A combinação de calor e umidade favorece a ocorrência de chuvas rápidas e isoladas em todas as regiões, principalmente à tarde. As temperaturas permanecem elevadas, com sensação de abafamento.

O domingo começa com muita nebulosidade e possibilidade de chuva rápida entre a madrugada e a manhã em algumas regiões. Ao longo do dia, o tempo abre e o sol aparece. Há previsão de pancadas de chuva à tarde no Sul e à noite na Grande Vitória e na Região Serrana. Nas demais regiões, não há previsão de chuva significativa.

articles.title: Prefeitura sanciona lei para uso de câmeras em escolas de BH | G1
articles.standfirst: Nova legislação vale apenas para espaços externos e proíbe videomonitoramento em ambientes internos, como salas de aula. Imagens deverão ser armazenadas de forma segura, com acesso restrito.
articles.summary: Sancionada pela Prefeitura, a lei de câmeras de segurança em escolas de BH foca no monitoramento externo e proíbe o uso de equipamentos em salas e banheiros.
articles.body:
Uma lei que incentiva a instalação de câmeras de segurança nas áreas externas das escolas municipais de Belo Horizonte foi sancionada pelo prefeito Álvaro Damião (União Brasil) e publicada na edição do Diário Oficial do Município (DOM) desta quinta-feira (19).

Conforme a prefeitura, a medida tem o objetivo de promover ações voltadas à proteção da comunidade escolar, incluindo estudantes, seus familiares e profissionais da educação. A mesma norma proíbe o uso do videomonitoramento em ambientes internos ( leia mais abaixo ).

O PL que deu origem à lei foi aprovado em segundo turno por unanimidade na Câmara Municipal de Belo Horizonte, com 37 votos favoráveis, no dia 9 de outubro.

Durante a votação, os vereadores acataram um substitutivo apresentado pelo líder do governo, Bruno Miranda (PDT). O texto reorganizou a proposta original e transferiu ao Poder Executivo, de forma geral, as responsabilidades pela implementação da política.

De autoria dos vereadores Maninho Félix (PSD) e Professora Marli (PP), a Lei 12.181, sancionada pelo prefeito, institui a Política Municipal de Segurança das Escolas Públicas da Rede Própria de Ensino.

A medida prevê a instalação de sistemas de videomonitoramento em locais como entradas, saídas e muros das escolas, com o objetivo de aumentar a segurança de estudantes, funcionários e moradores do entorno.

Por outro lado, a lei proíbe a instalação de câmeras em áreas internas das escolas , como salas de aula, banheiros, refeitórios e espaços de descanso.

Segundo o texto, as imagens deverão ser armazenadas em ambiente seguro e acessadas apenas por servidores autorizados. O compartilhamento do material só poderá ocorrer mediante decisão judicial, inquérito policial ou procedimento administrativo devidamente justificado.

Ainda de acordo com a lei, a comunidade escolar deverá ser informada, de forma clara e acessível, sobre a existência dos sistemas de monitoramento por meio de sinalização visível e de comunicação prévia aos pais ou aos responsáveis legais.

A legislação também autoriza a Prefeitura de Belo Horizonte a firmar convênios, parcerias e contratos para viabilizar a instalação, a manutenção e a fiscalização das câmeras, respeitando os limites orçamentários.

O texto, no entanto, não estabelece um prazo para o uso dos equipamentos nem determina que todas as escolas municipais recebam os aparelhos imediatamente.

articles.title: Piscinas do Parque Aquático de Cambuci transbordam após fortes chuvas | G1
articles.standfirst: Local está fechado há duas semanas e foi um dos pontos mais afetados pelo grande volume de água registrado nesta quinta-feira (19).
articles.summary: Local está fechado há duas semanas e foi um dos pontos mais afetados pelo grande volume de água registrado nesta quinta-feira (19).
articles.body:
As fortes chuvas que atingiram Cambuci , no Noroeste Fluminense, na manhã desta quinta-feira (19), provocaram o transbordamento das piscinas do Parque Aquático do município.

O local está fechado há duas semanas e voltou a ser atingido pelo grande volume de água.

O Parque Aquático foi um dos pontos mais afetados pela chuva, que atingiu principalmente a região da Serra de Natal.

Parque Aquático de Cambuci tem piscinas transbordadas durante temporal — Foto: Cambuci Notícias

O g1 procurou a Prefeitura de Cambuci, que informou aguardar uma avaliação da Secretaria Municipal de Obras para definir as medidas que serão adotadas.

O Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) emitiu um alerta amarelo de tempestade para municípios de Itaperuna, no Norte Fluminense, e outras cidades do Noroeste Fluminense. O aviso é válido até as 23h59 desta quinta-feira (19).

Entre os municípios incluídos no alerta estão Cambuci, Bom Jesus do Itabapoana, Italva, Aperibé e Itaocara.

A previsão indica chuva entre 20 e 30 milímetros por hora, podendo chegar a 50 milímetros ao longo do dia. Também são esperadas rajadas de vento entre 40 e 60 km/h e possibilidade de queda de granizo.

Segundo o Inmet, há baixo risco de alagamentos, queda de galhos de árvores, interrupções no fornecimento de energia elétrica e danos em plantações.

O instituto orienta que a população evite se abrigar debaixo de árvores, estacionar veículos próximos a placas de propaganda e torres de transmissão e utilizar aparelhos eletrônicos ligados à tomada durante as tempestades.

Em caso de emergência, a Defesa Civil pode ser acionada pelo telefone 199 e o Corpo de Bombeiros pelo 193 .

articles.title: Mogami vs Nilgiri: How Japan's frigates compare with India's warships
articles.summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh spent Wednesday morning aboard a warship that India may one day build for itself.
articles.body: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh spent Wednesday morning aboard a warship that India may one day build for itself. During his two-day visit to Japan, Singh visited the naval base at Yokosuka with his counterpart, Shinjiro Koizumi, and inspected the Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force's (JMSDF) Mogami-class frigate JS Natori. The two ministers also sailed aboard the vessel. Japan's defence ministry said the visit gave a significant opportunity to advance concrete maritime security cooperation and deepen trust between the two. Japan has recently signed a deal with eleven of these advanced frigates with Australia for around USD 7 billion.Japan has offered India the Mogami-class design plans and the option to build the 5,500-tonne frigates in Indian shipyards. The ships carry anti-ship and anti-aircraft missiles and torpedoes, and handle anti-submarine, anti-surface and air-defence roles, along with countermeasures against unmanned undersea mines. After the offer, Vice Admiral Ajay Kochhar visited Japan in October to look at cooperation in shipbuilding, mine countermeasures and joint development under 'Make in India'. He toured JS Mogami and held talks with Vice Admiral Yasuhiro Kunimi, the JMSDF's Vice Chief of Staff, and Lieutenant General Norimichi Shirakawa. JS Mogami also took part alongside INS Sahyadri in Exercise Malabar 2026, held from November 5 to 12 off Japan's Pacific coast.Two ways to build a frigateThe Mogami and India's Project 17A Nilgiri class are both multi-role stealth warships, but they reflect different needs. The Mogami is compact, with a standard displacement of about 3,900 tonnes and a full-load displacement of around 5,500 tonnes. It is about 133 metres long, can exceed 30 knots, and needs a crew of only about 90, since the design leans heavily on automation. Its armament includes a 127mm gun, eight anti-ship missiles, a 16-cell vertical launch system for the Type 03 surface-to-air missile and Type 07 anti-submarine rocket, and the SeaRAM close-in weapon system. For anti-submarine work it has variable-depth and towed-array sonar, torpedo tubes and a helicopter facility, and it is the only one of the two with dedicated mine-hunting capability. The Mogami class frigates are also equipped with the UNICORN (UNIted COmplex Radio Antenna) communications antenna array, which helps reduce the radar cross section of the ship.The Project 17A frigates are larger, at about 6,670 tonnes full load and 149 metres, with a top speed of around 28 knots and a complement of roughly 225. The strength of the Nilgiri class of vessels is the use of supersonic BrahMos anti-ship missiles, the MF-STAR radar, the Barak-8 medium-range air-defence system, a 76mm gun and anti-submarine rockets and torpedoes. They are a heavier platform with serious anti-ship strike and area air-defence capability, and about 75% of their content is indigenous.What's India's plan for its next class of frigatesProject 17B is expected to carry this progression further. The Ministry of Defence has identified indigenous weapons, fire-control systems and advanced electronic warfare as its key features, which could improve India's ability to detect, track and engage multiple threats while reducing dependence on imported combat systems. Its final specifications will decide how big a step it is.For now, the Mogami visit shows where both navies see value. Japan offers automation and mine warfare, India offers missile power and scale, and each is looking at the other's shipyards.

articles.body: Denmark’s parliament on Thursday unanimously ratified a security agreement with President Donald Trump covering Greenland, hoping to end a standoff over the Arctic island’s ⁠future that has rattled transatlantic relations. The U.S., Denmark and Greenland signed the agreement in September to resolve tensions after Trump repeatedly threatened to take control of the mineral-rich island, a self-governing Danish territory that is home to 57,000 people. The deal ⁠was backed by 109 Danish lawmakers ​and ⁠none voted against, the parliamentary tally showed. The deal is not subject to a vote by the Senate. The executive agreement ⁠will, following Thursday’s vote in Copenhagen, enter into force once the Danish ​foreign ⁠ministry informs the US in ‌a diplomatic note that procedures are complete. The deal expands the U.S. military’s role in Greenland, including permission to establish a “Golden Dome” missile defence system, while ‌reaffirming Danish sovereignty and Greenlanders’ right to self-determination. Trump’s ‌refusal to rule out military or economic force to acquire the island triggered a diplomatic crisis within NATO in January and forced Denmark and Greenland into months of intensive ⁠negotiations. Greenland’s parliament ratified the deal this month. Last week, it passed a first reading in Denmark’s parliament with backing from all parties, and lawmakers expressed relief and hope that the deal will normalize the situation in Greenland. “However, there are many indications that this is not an end, but rather a beginning,” said Mikkel Vedby Rasmussen, a political science professor ‌at the University of Copenhagen. “With the treaty in hand, the ​US will be able to demand greater influence on decisions ‌that have security policy implications and ⁠on part of the extraction of strategic resources,” he said. ⁠Other experts say the new agreement does not add much US military access to Greenland. The ‌shortest route from ​Europe to North America runs via strategically ‌located Greenland, where the northernmost ​US military base is already located.

articles.title: UN’s top court finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya
articles.summary: ICJ ruling is the first time a state has been found responsible for genocide at the court.
articles.body:
In a landmark verdict, the United Nations’ top court has ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Muslim minority Rohingya population in a brutal 2017 military crackdown that drove more than 730,000 Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh.

The ruling at the International Court of Justice (ICJ) at The Hague on Thursday is the first time a state has been found responsible for genocide at the court, and only the fourth time since the Nazi Holocaust that an international court ruled that the crime had been committed.

ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said the court, in a 9-6 decision, found that Myanmar “has committed genocide against the Rohingya group in northern Rakhine state, in violation of its obligations under the Genocide Convention”.

Evidence showed Myanmar forces killed at least 10,000 Rohingya people, Iwasawa said during a three-hour readout of the verdict.

“The Court finds that Myanmar’s security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence, as well as acts of extreme violence against children, and attacked fleeing Rohingya as they sought to flee in large numbers to Bangladesh,” he said.

In the specific cases that he referred to, Iwasawa said Myanmar had acted with “genocidal intent”.

The Special Advisory Council for Myanmar welcomed the judgement but stressed that the decision must lead to concrete accountability measures and reparations for victims.

Founding member Yanghee Lee said in a statement that it was a “deeply emotional day for all Rohingya people”, adding that “justice has been decided, but not yet delivered”.

“For decades, the Burmese military tried to erase our identity, deny our existence, and dismiss our suffering,” said Wai Wai Nu, executive director of the Women’s Peace Network and a former political prisoner.

“By finding that Myanmar committed genocide, ordering a guarantee of non-repetition, and ordering restitution and compensation, the world’s highest court has permanently shattered that state-sponsored lie,” she said.

Gambia, which brought the case to the court, called the ruling “a historic day for international justice” and urged Myanmar to comply “fully and without delay”.

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the United Kingdom would expel Myanmar’s defence attache and called for an urgent UN Security Council session to discuss the judgement.

Myanmar claimed its crackdown was in response to attacks on police posts by fighters from the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA).

The ICJ said that the “only reasonable inference” from evidence of widespread atrocities by Myanmar security forces is that they had the intent to destroy a “substantial part” of the Rohingya minority.

It said Myanmar should have known that there was a risk of genocide when armed civilians participated in the military campaign. “Myanmar thus violated its obligation to prevent genocide,” it added.

Myanmar is now obliged to provide reparations and restitution “as a result of Myanmar’s wrongful acts”, Iwasawa said.

The court said appropriate restitution by Myanmar would include facilitating the safe and voluntary return of Rohingya; returning or replacing all collective property damaged; facilitating the search for the disappeared and ensuring proper burials; providing for the physical and psychological rehabilitation of those mentally injured; and ensuring the population’s protection from persecution.

Reporting from the Hague, Al Jazeera’s Step Vaessen said the verdict is “extremely important for the Rohingya”.

“They’ve been waiting for 10 years for any kind of justice, but it’s also important for the whole international community because genocide is such a difficult act to prove.”

The hardest part of any genocide case is proving specific intent to destroy a group in whole or in part – an extremely high bar – said Toby Cadman, an international human rights lawyer. He noted that the ICJ had never before ruled that a state has specific intent to commit genocide.

“The court is guided by the genocide convention and what the genocide convention states, and it is a high threshold,” Cadman told Al Jazeera.

Human rights organisations welcomed the judgement. “We hope this ruling marks the beginning of a long overdue process of accountability in Myanmar,” Amnesty International said in a statement. It added that all crimes under international law “must be effectively investigated and those suspected of responsibility brought to justice”.

Cadman said that the situation does not come to an end with the ICJ’s ruling and a lot will depend on what comes next. This includes whether the issue goes before the UN Security Council and whether there are sanctions, or other remedies that the court can order to ensure it is enforced.

More than 1.3 million Rohingya remain displaced across South and Southeast Asia, including 1.2 million in sprawling refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar in Bangladesh, according to the UN. Conflict, shrinking humanitarian aid and dangerous sea crossings continue to leave many members of the community displaced and vulnerable.

images.caption: Rohingya refugee women with their children stand in line outside a food distribution centre at Balukhali refugee camp, about 50km (32 miles) from Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, on September 17, 2017, after fleeing Myanmar [Showkat Shafi/Al Jazeera]

articles.title: Sir James Cleverly named as Tory candidate in mayor of London 2028 race
articles.summary: The former home and foreign secretary has been a London Assembly member and fire authority chair.
articles.body:
Former home secretary and foreign secretary Sir James Cleverly has been selected as the Conservative candidate for mayor of London.

The MP for Braintree in Essex was chosen in a poll of party members in London, winning 86% of the vote.

Sir James saw off a challenge from Westminster City councillor Festus Akinbusoye and Richmond Park parliamentary candidate Sara Gezdari.

He said London's "best days are ahead if we make a change at the forthcoming election". The next mayoral election will be in May 2028.

Labour incumbent Lord Khan, first elected in 2016, is yet to confirm whether he will seek a fourth term.

Sir James, a former head of the London Fire Authority, was widely expected to win the nomination after he stood down from the shadow cabinet in August.

He said he would not seek re-selection as the candidate in his Essex seat at the next general election.

At the announcement of the result, he said Lord Khan was "letting London down".

Sir James added: "People are leaving London, or not choosing to come here in the first place - businesses, job creators, families leaving London - and by the time of the election in 2028, Khan will have been mayor for 12 years, and those two things are related.

"The problems London faces are the symptoms. Khan is the cause. When I ask Londoners, 'Do you feel safe walking home at night?', the answer is no."

"It's shameful, it's a failure, and it's not just crime.

"We have had the worst period of housebuilding since the Second World War and only the highest-earning Londoners can afford the cheapest houses in London."

Bridget Phillipson, chair of the Labour Party, said: "James Cleverly has a record of failure and now wants to inflict his disastrous CV on London.

"He backed a no-deal Brexit and Liz Truss's disastrous mini-budget, voted for cuts to policing and youth services and opposed action to clean up London's air.

"Londoners should never forgive and never forget the damage the Conservatives did to our capital."

Sir James, an Army reservist, represented the Tories on the London Assembly before his election as MP for Braintree in 2015.

After rising through the backbenches, he unsuccessfully ran for Conservative Party leader in 2024, losing out to Kemi Badenoch.

The only other confirmed party choice for the mayoral race is Laila Cunningham from Reform UK, whose candidacy was announced in January.

She told BBC London: "It's the Conservatives that cut police, they cut the magistrates' numbers, crime went up, they politicised stop and search, and as a result knife crime has gone up massively."

Sarah Olney and Rob Blackie are both candidates for the Liberal Democrats' nomination.

Olney, the MP for Richmond Park, told BBC London the city "really needs a champion but the Tories are not going to be able to effectively hold Labour to account given their record in the capital".

She added: "James Cleverley simply is not a credible contender for mayor of London.

"In the past decade he has enthusiastically championed Brexit and he was a huge supporter of Liz Truss's mini budget and both of those things have done so much damage to London."

Should Lord Khan decide not to run again, there are a number of London Labour figures with ambitions to be the next mayor, including MPs Dawn Butler and Rosena Allin-Khan.

The Green Party, which won outright control of three London boroughs at the local elections in May, leads minority administrations in Haringey and Lambeth, and runs Southwark in coalition with the Lib Dems, has yet to begin the process of picking a candidate for the 2028 mayoral race.

Mayor of Hackney Zoë Garbett, who was the Green candidate in the 2024 mayoral election, said Sir James would "take London backwards".

She added: "Cleverly's platform is all about dividing our communities and making people's lives harder and more expensive."

articles.title: Susan Smith denied parole as attorney says she ‘lost touch with reality’ on day she killed her sons
articles.summary: Susan Smith, the South Carolina mother convicted of drowning her two young sons in 1994, has been denied parole. During her hearing, her attorney argued that she had "lost touch with reality" on the day she killed 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alexander Smith.
articles.body: Susan Smith has been denied parole during a hearing more than 30 years after she killed her two sons by drowning them. She was convicted of two counts of murder in 1995 and sentenced to life in prison. While she was handed a life sentence, state law at the time allowed her to be considered for parole after serving 30 years. She faced a seven-person parole board in Columbia, South Carolina, on Thursday morning, when the board ruled against her. Smith is in prison for strapping her two young sons into her car and letting it roll into a lake, killing them in what prosecutors argued was a bid to win back a former lover who did not want children. She was sentenced to life in prison. During Thursday's hearing, Smith addressed the murders of her children and said she wants to live her life "to honor the memory of Michael and Alex." SUSAN SMITH'S EX-HUSBAND WANTS HER ‘IN PRISON UNTIL SHE DIES’ AFTER KILLING SONS IN ALLEGED BID TO WIN LOVER The two children, 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alexander, were killed on Oct. 25, 1994. Smith initially gave police a false account, alleging that a Black man had carjacked her and taken her two children. Her husband believed the story, and the couple appeared together on national television pleading for the return of their kids. "I know I promised them an unbearable pain. And I know that David didn't get to see Michael and Alex grow up. He didn't get to sit around a bike and school. And I'm really, really sorry for that. And I would go back and change all of that if I could, I would, but I can't. I'm not the same person I was 32 years ago. I have changed," Smith said. Her ex-husband, David Smith, pleaded with the parole board to keep his children's killer behind bars. CONVICTED SERIAL RAPIST ORIGINALLY SENTENCED TO 124 YEARS WALKS FREE AFTER 20, SPARKING OUTRAGE "So even though it's been 32 years, that doesn't take away what she did to Michael and Alex," David Smith said. "She took away one of the greatest gifts that God gives us in this life. She did that deliberately. It wasn't an accident. It wasn't a bad mistake. She did it deliberately." "And I know in my heart, granting parole would be a huge injustice to Michael and Alex," he added. During the parole hearing, Susan Smith's attorney, Tommy Thomas, read a statement from the convicted murderer in which she claimed she had "lost touch with reality" when she drowned her two young sons. "'My thoughts were not rational…I didn't, think, I understood that, I allowed this car to go into the lake,'" Thomas said. "She didn't understand the finality of what was going on. She said, ‘My thoughts were so screwed up at the time. And, I mean, I thought it was doing, what was best for my children. Because I believe that Jesus could take better care of them than I could.’" Tommy Pope, who is currently the speaker pro tempore for the South Carolina House of Representatives, prosecuted Smith previously told Fox News Digital that if released, the convicted murderer would get on social media and "love the attention." LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST "I think the difficulty is ... but I think the difficulty if Susan was out, she would be on social media," Pope said. "She would love the attention. It would be in David's face every day, and all he has ever talked about is justice for Michael and Alex." "[David Smith is] very good about not being vindictive towards Susan from a biblical standpoint. He says he's forgiven her. But he just thinks that justice ought to be served for those boys, and I fully agree," he added. CHARLES MANSON FOLLOWER TIED TO SHARON TATE MURDERS GETS RECOMMENDED FOR PAROLE AFTER 55 YEARS IN PRISON Pope said he believes Susan Smith, when she killed the children, wasn't sorry for killing them and said the jury intended on giving her an actual life sentence, not to be released on parole. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM THE FOX TRUE CRIME HUB "The jury truly believed they were giving her a life sentence, that she would spend the rest of her time lamenting what she'd done in regard to Michael and Alex. And I think what we've seen is, unfortunately, Susan is more focused on Susan," Pope said. "Her remorse is for her circumstances, not for those boys." SEND US A TIP Susan Smith was denied parole at her first hearing in November 2024, when she expressed regret for killing her sons. "I know that what I did was horrible. And I would give anything if I could go back and change it," she told the parole board through Zoom. "I love Michael and Alex with all my heart." "I am a Christian and God is a big part of my life. And I know he has forgiven me," she said. GET BREAKING NEWS BY EMAIL Pope, the person who prosecuted Smith, said he will be at every parole hearing to make sure she stays locked up. articles.title: Denmark parliament approves security deal with Greenland and US
articles.summary: All 109 Danish lawmakers present approved the deal, easing tensions over Trump’s desire to annex the Arctic island.
articles.body:
The Danish parliament ⁠has unanimously ratified a security agreement with the United States covering Greenland, aimed at bolstering security in the Arctic and North Atlantic.

Thursday’s decision to approve the deal signed in September eases tensions over US President Donald Trump’s desire to annex the Arctic island.

In the 179-seat parliament, known as the Folketing, the 109 members present voted in favour of the text, which was adopted without opposition or abstention.

The vote, which followed the second reading of the text, went through without any debate or opposition.

In early November, Greenland’s parliament had passed it by 16 votes, with seven abstentions.

The US, Denmark and Greenland signed the agreement in September to resolve tensions after Trump repeatedly threatened to take control of ⁠the mineral-rich island, a self-governing Danish territory home to 57,000 people.

The deal is not subject to a vote by the US Senate. The executive ‌agreement, following Thursday’s vote in Copenhagen, will enter into force once the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs informs the US in a diplomatic note that procedures are complete.

Signed in New York on September 22, the agreement supplements a 1951 accord on the US military presence in Greenland.

It allows the US to build two military bases in Greenland and blocks countries outside the European Union and NATO from strategic sectors, in order to stop China or Russia from gaining influence over the territory, particularly through investments.

Greenland is an autonomous territory of Denmark, but the deal is to remain in force even if Greenland gains full independence.

Since returning to the presidency in January 2025, Trump has repeatedly insisted that the US needed to control Greenland for strategic reasons, alarming NATO ally Denmark and other partners.

The shortest route ‌from ‌Europe to North America runs via strategically located Greenland, where the northernmost US military base is located.

articles.title: MARCA, superlíder digital: aventaja en 915.000 usuarios diarios y 451 millones de páginas vistas al mes al segundo
articles.standfirst: El mes de octubre refrenda el liderazgo de nuestra web según GfK: 3.328.258 de audiencia media diaria y más de 921 millones de páginas vistas al mes, el doble que su perseguidor
articles.summary: El mes de octubre refrenda el liderazgo de nuestra web según GfK: 3.328.258 de audiencia media diaria y más de 921 millones de páginas vistas al mes, el doble que su perseguidor
articles.body: El liderazgo diario de MARCA.com desde que empezaron a utilizarse medidores de audiencia digital en la prensa española sigue siendo incontestable e indiscutible. Nuestro sitio web es el más leído de España día tras día tanto en los medios deportivos como generalistas, según el informe correspondiente al mes de octubre elaborado por GfK, el medidor oficial de audiencias digitales del país, que sitúa a MARCA al frente en todas las métricas de calidad. Con una audiencia media diaria de 3.328.258 usuarios, MARCA se impone tanto a medios generalistas como deportivos. No hay ningún medio en España que supere la barrera de los tres millones de lectores diarios. Por detrás se sitúan El País con 2.479.831, As, que alcanza los 2.413.609 y OKdiario con 2.325.708. Por tanto, en audiencia media diaria MARCA aventaja en 915.000 usuarios al deportivo de Prisa. El liderazgo de MARCA también se refleja en el volumen total de consumo durante el mes de octubre, rozando los mil millones de páginas vistas (921.293.862). A gran distancia aparece As, segundo en este apartado con 470.615.062, es decir, a 451 millones de páginas vistas de MARCA, superlíder en consumo. Asimismo, MARCA destaca en otra de las métricas clave: la tasa de rebote. El medio deportivo de referencia en castellano en todo el mundo registra el menor porcentaje del mercado, con un 37%, lo que evidencia el alto nivel de interés y permanencia de los usuarios. En comparación, sus principales seguidores presentan cifras notablemente superiores: As alcanza el 52%, Mundo Deportivo el 45% y Sport el 47%. En sesiones, MARCA.com arrasa a sus competidores con sus 401 millones, más del doble que As (179) y muy por delante de MD (108) y Sport (52). Esta métrica revela la importancia de la recurrencia de visitas de los lectores de MARCA, mucho mayor que la competencia, hasta el punto que nuestra web suma más que los otros tres deportivos juntos. En redes sociales MARCA cuenta con muchos millones de seguidores más que el resto de medios españoles, tanto deportivos como generalistas. Es significativa la comparación con As, ya que la cuenta principal de MARCA suma 26,9 millones de seguidores por 12,9 de su perseguidor. Tanto en X como el Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, el canal de WhatsApp, y Threads el número de seguidores de MARCA es mucho mayor que el del resto de medios deportivos y generalistas.

articles.title: The Brexit debate is back - and there are nerves about what happens next
articles.summary: Many of the names and arguments that defined the Brexit period are emerging again, as the debate over the UK being part of the EU is back on the agenda.
articles.body:
"Stop Me If You Think You've Heard This One Before" sang Morrissey, as part of The Smiths in 1987, shortly before the band's acrimonious divorce.

It's a lyric Brexit veterans might be humming to themselves this week. Maybe even the prime minister, who is an avid fan of the Manchester band.

Some of the names - and arguments - that defined the Brexit period inside and outside Parliament are starting to emerge again, as the debate about the UK's relationship with the EU returns.

"It's like déjà vu with knobs on," said one veteran of the Leave campaign to us.

A new group called Stay Out has been set up, backed by figures who were part of the official Leave campaign in 2016. Boris Johnson has been back in the headlines, saying he still thinks Britons would choose to be outside the bloc.

Pro-EU groups such as the European Movement are raising their voices, pointing to the range of politicians, diplomats and academics they have supporting their argument. And a steady stream of Labour figures are now emerging to say they want to rejoin.

The former Deputy Prime Minister David Lammy made the argument on the BBC on Wednesday , saying Labour should go into the next election backing renegotiating membership of the EU and then putting that to people in another referendum.

He joins a list of cabinet ministers under Sir Keir Starmer who want to revisit EU membership; a list that includes former Chancellor Rachel Reeves, former Business Secretary Peter Kyle and former Welsh Secretary Jo Stevens. Others who served around Sir Keir's cabinet table think the same privately.

That is significant. Yes, they all backed Remain in 2016. But these are figures who were part of a government elected on a manifesto saying it was important to make Brexit work.

They set red lines in that manifesto because they thought the public had moved on. But they have now decided to say - most of them very publicly - that they think the picture has changed and the UK needs to think again.

The prime minister has opened the door to all options, from single market membership to rejoining the customs union to a referendum on full membership.

But in recent days, his language has softened a little from the clear commitment in his party conference speech that around the time of this Friday's summit he would "lay out to the country" the different options for Britain's long-term relationship with Brussels.

After some confusion about when this would take place, the government now says this will happen around the time that Burnham presents his 10-year plan, right before Parliament's Christmas break.

Burnham's allies say this will allow him to tie his EU policy more closely to his domestic agenda, arguing that a different arrangement with Europe would help with his other priorities such as the cost of living and re-industrialisation.

Others worry that the all-consuming nature of the EU debate means that it will drown out the other parts of the 10-year plan.

What remains unclear is the timeframe for the process that will follow Burnham setting out what he sees as the different Brexit options.

The prime minister has always been clear that Labour's commitments in its 2024 manifesto not to rejoin the single market or the customs union - let alone the EU altogether - still stand until the next general election.

And it was to those manifesto red lines that Burnham returned when asked about rejoining the EU at PMQs on Wednesday.

Yet those would not preclude Burnham initiating negotiations now on an arrangement breaking those red lines, which would take effect after the next general election.

Nevertheless, some on the prime minister's own side ponder that - having turned the volume up on the whole issue this autumn - he might be wise to turn it down a little in the new year, so it doesn't risk drowning out other things ministers want to talk about.

Andy Burnham is a prime minister who likes to explore things out loud. It's part of what he sees as a new way of doing politics, where he answers questions honestly and is prepared to discuss ideas while they are being formed, not just after they are a settled position.

It is a style that seeks to present a sense of a desired direction, even if some of the specifics end up being walked back from.

But even though it might be some time before the government has an official position on the future relationship, plenty of people are discussing what might happen next.

"It is all go again! My inbox is full of the same old stuff I thought I'd seen the back of years ago," one senior figure told us.

There are some nerves in the Labour Party about what might happen next. MPs who we have spoken to hold a range of views, which shows why this won't be plain-sailing.

Some are worried about re-opening the debate, calling it "toxic".

Others worry that the prime minister could disappoint pro-EU voters if he doesn't go far enough.

Others still wonder if the argument has changed enough that voters would decide differently in a new referendum.

"Both sides need fresh arguments, not the ones we all got tired of last time," said one.

"If this just looks like politicians wanting to rejoin because they never got over leaving then it's dead on arrival.

"If we can show that actually this is being led by businesses, by farmers, by different parts of society who need to rejoin because of the ways Brexit has harmed them, then it's a different matter," said another.

And what would the new EU the UK could rejoin look like?

Some Labour MPs ponder that the EU is changing – with the possibility of more right-wing leaders at the top table. They question whether they would want to be part of that.

EU-UK talks going down to the wire, says No 10

Burnham to set out options next month for long-term EU relationship

The EU that Burnham is eyeing up is very different to the one Britain left

UK lost more than it gained from Brexit, Burnham says ahead of EU summit

A long standing diplomat from an EU member state said that the possibility of political change within the EU, alongside the recent offer of associate membership to Canada and at least the possibility of a potential future arrangement with Ukraine after any peace deal, could mean Brussels becomes more open to looser forms of membership that it has not been willing to consider before.

But then there is Scotland. If the government backs another EU vote, some Scottish MPs worry it adds to the argument for another vote on Scottish independence.

Despite the warnings, plenty of MPs are delighted that the Europe debate is back on the agenda.

One summed it up like this: "It doesn't really matter to me at this point where the PM is heading on this – it's all good for appealing to progressive voters. Just being seen to talk about this even without it necessarily being clear what we're going to do is a big change from before."

That seems to be a prevailing mood at the moment. Lots of Labour MPs are happy the EU debate is back. But not all of them.

Andy Burnham will on Friday sign a new deal with the EU which ministers believe will drive economic growth and cut red tape for British businesses. It will be heralded as a new moment for the relationship.

But how much further could the reset go?

The government hasn't decided yet - but plenty of others have their own views.

articles.title: Susan Smith is denied parole again 32 years after drowning her sons in a South Carolina lake
articles.summary: COLUMBIA, S.C. — Susan Smith, who rolled her car into a South Carolina lake more than 30 years ago, killing her sons who were still strapped in their car seats, was denied parole again Thursday.
articles.body: COLUMBIA, S.C. — Susan Smith, who rolled her car into a South Carolina lake more than 30 years ago, killing her sons who were still strapped in their car seats, was denied parole again Thursday. Smith, 55, was sentenced to life in prison for the 1994 drownings of 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alex after the jury that convicted her chose not to give her the death penalty. But under South Carolina law at the time, she could ask for parole after 30 years and if refused, every two years after that. The parole board unanimously denied her parole request in 2024. The parole board voted unanimously Thursday to deny parole. Smith can ask for parole again in 2028. The boys’ father, David Smith, who vowed at the first hearing to oppose his ex-wife’s release as long as he can, and the original prosecutors in the case planned an early morning trip to Columbia to again ask that Smith remain in prison. Smith pinned to his jacket over his heart the same photo of his young sons that was once sent around the world when people thought they were kidnapped by a carjacker. David Smith asked the parole board to look into his heart. He said 32 years may seem like a long time, but to him it seems like it was yesterday when he buried his boys. He said he was there to advocate for his sons, who could never stand up for themselves. “She took away one of the greatest gifts God gives us — life. She did that deliberately. It wasn’t an accident, it wasn’t a mistake. She did it deliberately,” he said in testimony Thursday. Smith appeared by video before board that often rejects inmates Susan Smith’s hearing before the state Department of Probation, Parole and Pardon Services took place virtually with Smith joining by a video call from prison. She needed two-thirds support from the seven-member board to be released. Smith said her sons were innocent children who did not deserve to die. She said she has so much remorse for killing them and asked the board to give her a chance to get out of prison and do good for the world. She cried at her first hearing, but not on Thursday. “I know that David didn’t get to see Michael and Alex grow up. You didn’t get to see him ride a bike or go to school. And I’m really, really sorry for that, and I would go back and change all of that if I could, I would, OK? I’m not the same person I was 32 years ago,” Smith said. Odds for parole were against her. The board granted parole in only 4% of cases before it and the majority were in non-violent cases, according to the agency’s statistics. And Smith’s case is one of the most notorious cases to come before the board. She made international headlines in 1994 when she insisted for nine days that a Black carjacker drove away with her sons when the boys were at the bottom of John D. Long Lake in Union County. The claims by Smith, who is white, played into a centuries-old racist trope of Black men being a danger to white women and stoked concerns about crime that were prevalent in 1990s America and remain so today. Prosecutors blamed affair while defense blamed mental health Prosecutors have long argued that Smith killed her sons because she believed they were the reason the wealthy son of the owner of the business where she worked broke off their affair. “Susan made the choice out of selfishness. She really thought she could start her life over with someone else by getting rid of these children,” said Tommy Pope who was a prosecutor at Smith’s trial. Smith and her attorneys blamed her mental health at her trial 30 years ago, saying she planned to go into the lake with her sons but changed her mind at the last moment. Her lawyer said Thursday she has no other criminal history and would be a low risk to ever commit a crime again. Psychologist Jessie Hill said at the parole hearing Smith’s roiling mental illness has been greatly subdued thanks to medicine, hormonal changes from menopause and the deaths of her mother and stepfather, who admitted in court he sexually abused his stepdaughter from before she was a teenager. Pope said she relished attention when she lied about her children being kidnapped for nine days and has continued to do so behind bars, trying to find relationships with men or capitalize on the fame that came from being notorious and a true crime sensation. Pope said David Smith has told him he always worried about seeing his ex-wife in the grocery store if she was released. Pope said in today’s society it would be even worse. “If you think this family’s been through hell now, imagine every day if you pick up your phone or you turn on your computer and there’s Susan talking because you know the letters that have been written, there are people out there that idolize Susan,” Pope said. Smith made tearful pleas for days before confessing For nine days in 1994, Smith made numerous and sometimes tearful pleas asking that Michael and Alex be returned safely. But she would eventually confess. A re-creation by investigators showed it took six minutes for Smith’s Mazda to dip below the surface, while cameras inside the vehicle showed water pouring in through the vents and steadily rising. The boys’ bodies were found dangling upside-down in their car seats, one tiny hand pressed against a window.

articles.title: UK joins in GTA 6 frenzy as game becomes available worldwide
articles.summary: The game, which was in development for 13 years, is set become one of the world's most popular entertainment products ever.
articles.body:
After years of anticipation and delays, as well as controversy around worker rights, Grand Theft Auto 6 has completed its phased worldwide release and is available to gamers everywhere, including the UK.

There has been near universal praise from critics, with review aggregator Metacritic calculating its average score at 99 out of 100 based on 150 reviews.

Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time has held the top spot since 1998 - but Metacritic confirmed to the BBC that this has now officially been overtaken.

GTA 6 is set to become one of the world's most popular entertainment products ever, with fans booking time off work, and schools warning students not to bunk off.

Some schools have reminded parents and pupils to prioritise study over the game, which has an 18 rating for "strong graphic violence, strong sexual themes and use of illegal drugs".

One school in Essex incentivised pupils to attend with prize s such as vouchers, Christmas dinners and a pass to skip the lunch queue.

The UK rating means it can only be legally sold to an adult. It does not stop an adult letting their child play the game - instead it is meant to inform their decision.

The game, set in the fictional US state of Leonida, follows two protagonists, Lucia and Jason, through the seedy underbelly of America after an "easy score goes wrong".

It was released at midnight in all the countries it is available in, which meant New Zealanders were the first to access it.

"The graphics are great. Even from the set-up and credits, it's feeling pretty good," Aleana Fernando, who lives in Auckland, New Zealand, told BBC Newsbeat soon after she started playing.

Once the game was released at midnight UK time, gamers were equally enthralled by the game's graphics and attention to detail.

Charlie Wood from London said he had "already laughed at the dialogue before even stepping into the gameplay".

About 30 minutes into playing in Leonida, he said it was "most definitely worth the wait".

Meanwhile in Germany, Timur told the BBC he was impressed by how lifelike the game was.

"It really feels like a life simulation with the amount of in-game encounters," he said.

The Guardian's Keza MacDonald was impressed by the relationship between the main characters.

"GTA has never been particularly kind to women... there is still a lot of sexism in GTA VI's world, but now we have Lucia to react to it," she said.

"This is the first GTA in which I have felt the women are treated as people, not only Lucia but also the many other female characters in the story".

After GTA 5 became one of the most successful entertainment products of all time - with estimates of net profits soaring as high up as $10bn (£7.6bn) - anticipation could not be higher for the sixth instalment.

Makers Rockstar North, headquartered in Edinburgh, delayed the release twice, saying it needed extra months to finish the game with the level of polish fans had come to "expect and deserve".

The company was also set back by hacks and leaks of its unfinished version.

On Monday, 21-year-old Arion Kurtaj, from Oxford, pleaded guilty to the Rockstar Games hack and a handful of others which he carried out when he was 16 and 17 years old with the hacking gang Lapsus$.

He stole internal company data including 90 clips showing nearly 60 minutes of gameplay from the unfinished and hugely anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6.

A group of Rockstar workers who were sacked by the company have also been protesting outside its offices, ahead of a tribunal which heard they were penalised for discussing working conditions in a private online forum while working on the game.

They claimed they were punished for being part of a workers' union, but Thomas Cordrey, representing Rockstar, said employees made disparaging comments about the company on a semi-public Discord server and shared confidential information.

Players were able to download the 212GB game ahead of time, in order to be able to play it as soon as it was made available.

Some had even gone to the lengths of buying a whole new console dedicated to the game.

Broadband providers Virgin Media O2, as well as BT and EE, said internet traffic records had been broken in the days leading up to the UK release.

The BBC has heard from people planning to take time off work - as well as a company which has given its employees the day off - in order to dedicate time to the game.

Kieran Youens-Byrne, 34, from Manchester said he was "going on a pilgrimage to Wales" where he would be "completely off grid" for a week.

He added his partner Clare "has been incredibly understanding, although I suspect she's questioning why our romantic getaway revolves around a PlayStation".

articles.title: A 'Muslim-only' event at a waterpark in Texas was canceled in June. Now organizer Aminah Knight sues Greg Abbott and the city of Grand Prairie over religious discrimination
articles.summary: A Texas woman who organized a Muslim Eid celebration at a taxpayer-funded waterpark has sued Governor (outgoing) Greg Abbott and the city of Grand
articles.body: A Texas woman who organized a Muslim Eid celebration at a taxpayer-funded waterpark has sued Governor (outgoing) Greg Abbott and the city of Grand Prairie, accusing them of religious discrimination after the event was canceled following the governor's intervention. Dr Aminah Knight, who organized the annual Epic Eid celebration at the city-owned EPIC Waters Indoor Waterpark, filed a federal lawsuit on November 17 through the Council on American-Islamic Relations and its Texas chapter.The lawsuit alleged that Abbott abused his executive authority by threatening to withhold $530,000 in public safety grants from Grand Prairie unless officials canceled the June 1 event. It claimed that the governor's actions violated Knight's First Amendment rights and singled out Muslims for exercising their religious freedoms.The controversy erupted after promotional flyers described the event as being for Muslims only. The announcement, which also specified a modest dress code and halal food, triggered backlash on social media, with critics questioning why a taxpayer-funded facility was hosting an event that appeared to exclude people of other faiths.Abbott pressured Grand Prairie to cancel the celebration and commit to never allowing a similar event again, threatening to withdraw $530,000 in state grants if it failed to comply. Knight later clarified that people of all faiths were welcome, provided they followed the modest dress code. But the event was already canceled after Abbott's intervention.The organizer claimed the waterpark had previously hosted the celebration without controversy for two years, attracting more than 600 attendees in 2025. She also alleged that she had fulfilled her contractual obligations and that the waterpark's explanation for the cancellation, a missing deposit, was unfounded.Dr Aminah Knight is a 43-year-old mother of six, former New York teacher and daycare and preschool director in the suburbs of Fort Worth. She said her idea was to allow Muslim families to celebrate at a water park without feeling out of place because of their full-coverage swimwears.The lawsuit has named Abbott, Grand Prairie and the waterpark operator as defendants. It has sought an injunction preventing the governor from pressuring the city to block future Muslim celebrations at the venue and asks that Knight be allowed to organize another Eid event in 2027.Knight has also sought compensation for lost revenue, ticket refunds and legal expenses.CAIR argued that other religious groups, including Christian organizations, have been allowed to hold private events at the waterpark without similar objections.The lawsuit came amid a broader legal dispute between Abbott and CAIR. Just a day before the filing, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton dropped a separate lawsuit seeking to prevent the Muslim civil rights organization from operating in the state.You use AI every day. articles.title: Two years in, Dutch church’s nonstop service shields family seeking asylum
articles.summary: Under Dutch law, police cannot enter a church as long as a religious service is taking place.
articles.body:
Kampen, Netherlands – “We have traded our freedom for safety,” said Aram Babayants.

The 22-year-old, his parents and three younger sisters have been living in a church in Kampen, the Netherlands, to avoid deportation to Uzbekistan. They have not set foot outside for more than 700 days.

With the help of thousands of volunteers, the Open Hof Protestant church has been holding a nonstop service, day and night, since November 21, 2024. A Dutch law that prevents authorities from interrupting a religious service enables this so-called “church asylum”.

The Babayants family of six has been in the Netherlands for 13 years. The youngest children, Amelia, 12, and five-year-old Aleksa were born here, while 16-year-old Ariana said she has no memories of her time in Uzbekistan.

“This is the only country we know to be home,” Ariana told Al Jazeera.

While the family is grateful for the support of churches and volunteers, the circumstances have taken a toll, physically and mentally.

“The days often look the same,” Ariana said.

Every weekday, volunteer teachers come to the church to lead high school classes. But Ariana misses being in a classroom, seeing her friends and running “really fast” outdoors, in nature. To connect to peers, she and her sister Amelia started a TikTok account where they post dance videos.

“We are locked up, even though we have done nothing wrong,” Ariana said.

Before taking refuge in Open Hof, the family lived in various refugee centres. In 2014, they applied for asylum in the Netherlands on the grounds that the father, Alexandr, feared persecution in Uzbekistan.

But their asylum applications have repeatedly been rejected.

“It is not about the asylum procedure,” said Herman Stompers, a coordinator of the church asylum. “This is about children’s rights.”

It is “absurd” that children who are rooted here, who speak the language and have been living here for many years, are at risk of deportation, Stompers said. Though children’s rights are anchored in family law and criminal law, they are not an integral part of Dutch immigration law, suggesting that “children’s rights only apply to white, Dutch children”.

It’s not a church’s job to get involved politically, he added, but “when politics falls below the baseline of human dignity, you have to do something”.

Stompers emphasised that the issue goes beyond the Babayants family. The church and volunteers advocate for the enshrinement of the rights of all children in Dutch law. The latest government figures show there are about 420 children in the Netherlands who have been awaiting asylum approval for more than five years.

When pastor Kasper Jager got the call, on October 28, 2024, asking if his church could host the Babayants family, he knew he had to say yes. After seeking approval from the other parishes in Kampen as well as the Dutch church council, he found overwhelming support. Three weeks later, the family moved in.

Although some other churches denounced the move as excessive activism, Jager said he is simply following an example. “Jesus was an activist. He was all about standing up for the most vulnerable,” he said.

The fact that the Babayants family are Christian is a “coincidence”, according to Jager, who said the church would have done the same for a Muslim family. “It is about justice and humanity,” he said.

More than 2,000 volunteers, both religious and non-religious, have filled the service schedule with prayers, sermons and hymns for the past two years. They travel from across the country, and sometimes even from abroad, to participate. At least three people are needed during each two-hour block, adding up to about 50 volunteers per day.

The solidarity shown towards the Babayants family is in sharp contrast to the rising anti-migrant sentiment felt across the Netherlands. Recent months have seen a wave of anti-immigration protests, with far-right demonstrators chanting racist slogans, throwing fireworks at authorities and attacking refugee accommodation centres.

In February, a minority government led by progressive Prime Minister Rob Jetten took office, replacing the most right-wing government in the country’s history.

There was hope that the new, centre-right government would ensure the rights of so-called “rooted children”, who have spent most of their lives in the country or were born here, but this has not been the case, pastor Jager said. “Politically, not much is happening,” he added.

In July, the highest administrative court in the Netherlands ruled that three families should be given residence permits, putting the children’s rights above the government’s aim to limit migration numbers.

Pastor Jager is “cautiously optimistic”, hoping the ruling will set a precedent. But even if it does, he warned it could take years before the Babayants family can safely leave the church.

A previous church asylum case in The Hague that the pastor was involved in lasted 96 days. No one expected the Babayants’ case to go on as long as it has, he said.

“Of course, we can’t keep doing this forever,” coordinator Stompers told Al Jazeera. How much longer they can continue depends entirely on the church community, the volunteers and, first and foremost, the family itself. “As long as they can keep going, we can, too.”

Aram and Ariana want nothing more than to close this chapter and “finally start living”.

“We want to participate [in society], but we can’t,” Aram told Al Jazeera. When asked what he wishes his future to look like, Aram replied: “My dream is to get one of those blue letters from the tax office. That would mean I am allowed to stay.”
