articles.body: President Donald Trump issued a joint "peace declaration" with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday following the trio's trilateral meeting during the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China. "The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security," the White House said in a statement, titled "U.S.-Russia-China Heads of State Declaration toward Peace." Russia's Foreign Ministry and China's Chamber of Commerce to the EU confirmed the pact in near-identical statements, which also highlighted the three countries' commitment to reducing nuclear proliferation, increasing global petroleum production and upholding international institutions. TRUMP'S HISTORIC SUMMIT WITH XI, PUTIN MARKS DIPLOMATIC MILESTONE, BUT BREAKTHROUGHS REMAIN ELUSIVE "The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows," each of the U.S., Chinese and Russian statements read. China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs also released a more expansive statement on the meeting. TRUMP'S CHINA TRIP: HISTORIC XI-PUTIN TALKS, 'SUPERINTELLIGENCE' BOAST AND OTHER TOP MOMENTS "President Xi noted that it is a groundbreaking move for the top leaders of China, Russia and the United States to hold the first-ever meeting in history. History tells us that peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos in the world. Peace has been an enduring pursuit of humanity," the statement read. The statement referred to the theme of the historic meeting between the three leaders, the first time in history the three nations' heads of state met collectively, as "Safeguarding World Peace and Promoting Strategic Stability in Major-Country Relations." CHINA'S XI SURPRISES TRUMP AT TARMAC, RECIPROCATING GESTURE SHOWN MONTHS AGO "More than 80 years ago, China, Russia and the United States, the key anti-fascist forces in the world, fought shoulder to shoulder and achieved great victories, winning peace and tranquility for the world. History is the best textbook; we must remember history, and learn from it to shape the future," the Chinese statement continued. TRUMP CANNOT DETER XI AND PUTIN’S NUCLEAR GOALS WITH A STRATEGY DESIGNED FOR JUST ONE All three countries' statements affirmed a commitment to nuclear harm reduction, with each including language stating that "a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought." Additionally, China's readout of the meeting stated that President Trump noted how many eyes around the world would be on the summit. KIM JONG UN'S NUCLEAR BUILDUP SPARKS 'SERIOUS CONCERN' AHEAD OF TRUMP-XI-PUTIN SUMMIT "President Trump noted that the U.S.-China-Russia summit draws attention from across the world. It is very important and has made history. The three countries are all nuclear-weapon states, and have a special and important responsibility to safeguard world peace and stability," the Chinese statement read. An earlier Chinese readout of the meeting revealed topics covered on the agenda, which included Russia's war in Ukraine, ongoing tension in the Middle East and the Korean Peninsula. articles.title: France awaits verdict six years after police beat Black music producer
articles.summary: Three officers are accused of assaulting Michel Zecler in an incident that was filmed by surveillance cameras.
articles.body:
Paris, France – Six years ago, Michel Zecler was assaulted by the three officers at his Parisian music studio.

Surveillance camera footage shows the officers pushing Zecler, who is Black, inside his studio and beating him until other musicians intervened on November 21, 2020.

Aurelien Lapersonne, Pierre Plantier and Philippe Tondeux are accused of striking the music producer 29 times in four minutes, and an additional six times in the face after Zecler was already handcuffed.

The case fuelled wider concerns in France about police brutality and caught the public’s attention. At the time, football star Kylian Mbappe shared an image of a heavily injured Zecler, blood running from his face, with the words: “Unbearable video. Unacceptable violence”.

The three French police officers are also accused of forging a public document.

During the attack, the officers allegedly made multiple racist remarks towards Zecler. All three signed a falsified police report stating that Zecler hit the police officers – a claim refuted by surveillance footage.

“It’s pretty obvious that this case is about institutional racism, systemic discrimination and police violence. Everything is connected. Not only are we dealing with police violence against a Black man, but that’s on top of attempting to conceal evidence and falsify a report,” Rim-Sarah Alouane, a legal scholar and an associate researcher in public law at the University of Toulouse Capitole, told Al Jazeera. “When these reports are falsified, we’re questioning the integrity of the entire system.”

The prosecution’s office requested a permanent ban on all three officers, along with prison sentences.

The prosecutor called for a jail sentence of six years without parole for Lapersonne, the officer who initiated the police identity check and submitted the falsified report, a five-year sentence for the trio’s leader, Tondeux, the most experienced officer present, and four years for the third police officer, Plantier.

“There is no room for a symbolic sentence,” a representative of the public prosecutor’s office said in a statement. “We are talking about crimes, violence and racial slurs. About a complete lack of control over what was done and an absolute determination to get away with it in the end.”

‘If there was no footage, we would not be here today’

A series of court cases has identified the systemic discrimination among the police in France.

Last year, the European Court of Human Rights condemned France for racial profiling of Karim Touil, a young French national of North African origin who was stopped by police three times within 10 days in November and December 2011.

In October 2023, France’s high court acknowledged racial profiling during police identity checks but did not require French authorities to take the “necessary measures to end this longstanding, abusive practice”, Human Rights Watch (HRW) noted.

In 2021, the French government was condemned for “gross negligence” in an identity check of three high school students in at Gare du Nord in Paris.

Although concerns about police violence in France are not new, this trial is pivotal because of the surveillance footage and attempted cover-up, Alouane noted.

“This trial brings to light those issues that human rights organisations have been documenting for years. It gives an illustration, through a proper case, about the use of force and systemic violence that we’ve known about for years,” Alouane said. “If there was no footage, we would not be here today. The police would have gotten away with it.”

Police officer Lapersonne, who submitted the report, initially claimed that Zecler attacked the officers and “struck out with his arms and legs”. When the presiding judge asked if he had “made that up”, Lapersonne responded, “Absolutely.” Lapersonne’s initial police report also failed to mention that the officers landed blows on Zecler.

“I deliberately omitted them. I think out of fear. It was stupid of me,” Lapersonne told the presiding judge.

For Alouane, this case revealed the tactics behind systemic police violence in France.

“The falsified documents aspect is crucial to illustrate why this case advanced and the public attention it received. In this case, the footage directly contradicted the police’s claims. The cops knew they did something wrong,” she said. “This is a serious accusation and not an isolated incident.”

The trial comes as France’s Senate considers a controversial bill that would presume police officers and gendarmes acted in self-defence when using firearms in the line of duty, which would place the burden of proof on the complainant. Critics call the proposal a “licence to kill”. The National Assembly approved the measure in July.

“It’s a very dangerous piece of legislation. It’s liberticide. It would create a sense of impunity amongst police officers — which already exists, but this would strengthen that. It would undermine investigations and make access to the justice system even more difficult for victims and their families,” Alouane said. “It raises serious issues regarding equality under the law because it puts a presumption of innocence in favour of people because of their profession as cops.”

Legislation like the self-defence law could inhibit cases like Zecler’s in the future, Alouane noted.

“If this proposal were in place, we would not have this case. It would have been dismissed today,” she said.

French police are also under scrutiny for their tactics during recent student protests. A 15-year-old lost a hand from a police stun grenade, and another officer threw a tear gas canister at close range, shattering a 14-year-old’s jaw and several teeth.

articles.title: Save the Children: Gaza’s children face ‘unmatched dangers’
articles.summary: Aid group says one third of violations against children worldwide were in occupied Palestinian territory.
articles.body:
Children in Gaza face dangers “unmatched” anywhere in the world after three years of war, with at least 20,000 killed, according to the aid group Save the Children.

The warning came in the group’s annual global report on Thursday – the same day Israel’s military told the AFP news agency it had finished a ground operation in central Gaza that began a day earlier, despite a “ceasefire” that took effect more than a year ago.

Save the Children said almost one third of the tens of thousands of attacks and violations against children recorded worldwide last year took place in the occupied Palestinian territory.

It counted nearly 12,500 cases – mostly attacks on hospitals and schools, and denial of aid.

“This report is showing very clearly that what happened and what continues to happen in Gaza are violations at a scale that we haven’t seen,” Regional Director Ahmad Alhendawi told the AP news agency.

He said conditions have shown little improvement this year, and that many surviving children are injured and have lost their parents.

The report found that denial of humanitarian aid is the fastest-growing violation against children worldwide. Verified incidents rose from 509 in 2015 to 8,322 in 2025 – almost one per hour on average – and more than 70 percent of them targeted Palestinian children.

Killings and maimings made up the largest share of violations since 2005, with 171,712 verified cases, and more than 70 percent were recorded in four countries, plus the occupied Palestinian territory.

Gaza’s Health Ministry said at least 300 children have died while waiting for Israeli permission to leave for life-saving treatment, including at least 90 with cancer. Another 5,400 are on medical travel lists awaiting approval. In February, it reported that 1,360 patients had died awaiting permits since the Rafah crossing between Gaza and Egypt closed in May 2024.

Displaced resident Riad Abou Shamel, 65, told AP that Gaza’s children “are deprived of the bare minimum in life”.

“They go to the market and can barely bring back half a cucumber or half an apple,” he said.

Israel’s military told AFP that its first broad ground offensive since a “ceasefire” was signed more than a year ago “is complete”.

The new operation was launched in central Gaza on Wednesday, and went beyond the “Yellow Line” to dismantle a tunnel the Israelis claimed posed an “immediate and direct threat” to its troops.

The “Yellow Line” demarcates the Israeli-occupied area of Gaza, and was established under the truce agreed by Israel and Hamas in October 2025.

Hamas called the two-day operation a “blatant ceasefire violation”.

More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the “ceasefire” began, according to an AFP tally of Gaza Health Ministry data.

Israel did not immediately comment on Save the Children’s report, the AP said.

He challenged the final list, alleging that certain candidates who were not included in the original list of candidates called for document verification had subsequently been allowed to participate in the sports trials and were included in the selection process.Govt informed the court that the recruitment board had issued a notice on Nov 3, 2025, allowing candidates who had failed to submit relevant documents along with their application forms to furnish them within three days. articles.title: Mick Jagger stayed at an 1830s Australian homestead in 1969 while filming Ned Kelly; 57 years later, the 610-hectare estate is for sale after its owners restored a creek to reduce erosion and recharge groundwater
articles.summary: A 610 hectare estate in Mulloon, on the New South Wales Southern Tablelands, has come to market after nearly three decades under the same family.
articles.body: A 610 hectare estate in Mulloon, on the New South Wales Southern Tablelands, has come to market after nearly three decades under the same family. Palerang Homestead is where Mick Jagger stayed in 1969 while filming Ned Kelly, and its history is now paired with a modern restoration project aimed at protecting the land, according to Domain and Zango.The property was originally established in the 1830s as Hyland’s Retreat, a stagecoach inn connecting Sydney and Goulburn to the Monaro. Today, it is being offered either as a combined 610 hectare holding or as two separately titled parcels, giving buyers a choice in how they approach the sale.A homestead with a music storyJagger came to nearby Braidwood to play Ned Kelly in Tony Richardson’s film of the same name. During part of the production, Palerang Homestead became home to Jagger and members of the film crew. Jagger and his then partner, the late British singer Marianne Faithfull, stayed at the property. The estate became part of the story behind one of the Rolling Stones’ most recognisable songs.During filming, a prop pistol exploded and injured Jagger’s hand. While recovering, he picked up a guitar and began working on a new song, which later became “Brown Sugar.”How the song came to lifeJagger later confirmed that he wrote “Brown Sugar” while filming Ned Kelly in Australia. Local history places the writing of the song at Palerang.In a 1995 interview with Rolling Stone, Jagger said he was trying to rehabilitate his hand and had a new kind of electric guitar. He described playing in the middle of the outback and writing the tune.The song was released on The Rolling Stones’ 1971 album Sticky Fingers. The album has sold and been streamed more than 22 million times, according to Domain.What the estate includesThe property includes a two storey workshed, garden shed, and a two storey “Stables.” The homestead itself has six bedrooms and three bathrooms, according to the listing details. The land supports commercial scale grazing across native pastures. Roughly 65 percent of the property is considered arable for cropping, which adds to its agricultural value. The estate is being sold through an expression of interest campaign. The sale offers buyers the chance to own a piece of Australian history as well as a working rural property.Why the restoration mattersCurrent owners Sue and Ulli Tuisk have spent 28 years on the property. They worked with the Mulloon Institute to implement an engineered leaky weir system along Mulloon Creek. The system is designed to recharge groundwater, reduce erosion, and preserve lush pastures during dry periods. The work has been recognised globally by the United Nations.Ulli Tuisk said the rehydration of Mulloon Creek was the biggest renovation project the owners undertook. The effort reflects a broader focus on land health and long term sustainability.What comes nextThe sale of Palerang Homestead marks the end of an era for the Tuisk family. After 28 years, they are passing on a property that has both a cultural past and a practical future. For buyers, the estate offers more than just land. It combines a historic homestead, a working farm, and a restoration project that has already earned international recognition.Whether the property is sold as one large holding or split into two parcels, its story is likely to attract attention. The mix of music history, rural scale, and environmental work makes it a rare offering in the New South Wales market.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Senate Republicans in US reject measure to limit Trump’s war powers in Iran
articles.summary: The resolution was defeated 51-48. Three Republicans broke rank, voting against the measure.
articles.body:
United States Senate Republicans have voted against a measure that would have required President Donald Trump to end the war in Iran or seek congressional approval to continue military action, reaffirming their support for the conflict despite recent electoral losses widely attributed in part to public opposition to the war.

The resolution was defeated on Thursday 51 to 48. Senators voted largely along party lines. In June, the House of Representatives passed it 215 to 208.

Three Republicans – Susan Collins of Maine, Lisa Murkowski of Alaska and Rand Paul of Kentucky – voted with Democrats in favour of the measure. Only one Democrat, Senator John Fetterman of Pennsylvania, voted against it.

Democratic Senator Tim Kaine of Virginia, a longtime advocate for restoring Congress’s constitutional authority over decisions to go to war, urged lawmakers to support the resolution. He argued that the election results reflected widespread dissatisfaction with the conflict and the rising cost of food, fuel and other goods.

“The unpopularity was made absolutely, manifestly clear in the election results of November 3,” Kaine said ahead of the vote.

articles.title: UNFPA puts India's population at 1.47 billion in 2026, calls for investment in 'youth dividend'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Continuing to be the most populous country in the world, India’s population for 2026 is estimated to be 1.47 billion (147.66) crores with the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Continuing to be the most populous country in the world, India’s population for 2026 is estimated to be 1.47 billion (147.66) crores with the population doubling time of 81 years, according to the UNFPA’s State of The World Population Report 2026 released on Thursday. India’s population is expected to grow to about 1.7 billion (170 crores) before it begins to fall, around 40 years from now.India’s population was 1.46 billion in 2025, 1.44 billion in the year before that. More than one in four Indians are aged 10 to 24, the report highlights citing it to be India’s “youth moment” and calling for investing while the dividend window is open.Surpassing China, India became the world’s most populous country with 142.86 crore people in 2023 with China falling behind India with a population of 142.57 crore.Meanwhile, China’s estimated mid - year population for 2026 stands at 1.41 billion (141.29 crores) with 70% of the population in the 15-64 years bracket. 15% of China’s population is 65 and above. Fertility rate stands at 1.0 and life expectancy is high at 76 for men and 82 for women.The demographic indicators show that in India those in the 0-14 years age group account for 24% of the population; for 10-19 years this is 17% and for 10-24 it is a strong 26% reflecting India’s youth dividend. The data shows that 69% of India’s population is in the 15-64 years bracket and the population aged 65 and older account for 8%.Life expectancy for males is 71 years and that for females is 74. If one looks at world population in 2026 it is estimated at 8.3 billion with population doubling time 84 years. Globally life expectancy at birth stands at 71 for men and 76 for women.The report, flags India’s Total Fertility Rate at 1.9, the same as last year, which is below the replacement level fertility of 2.1 births per woman indicating that women are having fewer children than needed to maintain the population size from one generation to the next.The 2026 report also draws on UNFPA’s global Demographic Futures Survey of more than 108,000 internet-connected adults in 73 countries, including 1,722 in India to highlight aspirations around relationships, parenthood and life goals, and the conditions that influence people’s ability to realise them.It further states that young people’s aspirations regarding family and relationships will play a central role in shaping the nation’s demographic trajectory.Survey findings from India show that optimism runs high with 83% of respondents feeling positive or very positive about the future, despite concerns about conflict, economic insecurity and inequality, UNFPA highlights. Women aged 18 to 39 describe an ideal family size of 2.1 children and parenthood remains a strong aspiration: nearly 85% of childless respondents aged 35 to 39 would ideally like to become parents.“Young people need confidential, non-judgmental ‘Sexual Reproductive Health’ information and services (contraception, menstrual health, STI prevention, referral) alongside pre-pregnancy, maternal and postnatal care,” UNFPA states while emphasising the need for India to expand and strengthen youth-responsive primary care.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: Authorities are releasing new video, captured by a passing MTA bus, showing the moment a multi-story building collapsed in Brooklyn last week, killing eight people and injuring 18.
articles.body: Authorities are releasing new video, captured by a passing MTA bus, showing the moment a multi-story building collapsed in Brooklyn last week, killing eight people and injuring 18. The bus was in service, on its B103 route, when the Nov. 11 collapse happened, according to the MTA, which posted the video on its YouTube page. The footage shows the vehicle apparently stopped at a light. The building starts to fall apart as the light changes, and the bus moves through a cloud of dust as it passes by. Authorities identified the dead, which included two children, in the hours after the collapse. As of the most recent update, only one of the injured patients remained in critical condition. There was no immediate update on that individual Thursday. Meanwhile, the Department of Buildings said Wednesday the collapse at 1321 Flatbush Avenue on Nov. 11 caused so much damage to the adjacent building, it too will have to come down. And the people who live there won’t even be allowed inside to retrieve their belongings, due to stability- and asbestos-related concerns. The vacate orders for other neighboring buildings, including 1325 and 1327 Flatbush Avenue, remained in place as of Wednesday, the DOB said. The building at 1325 Flatbush Avenue will have shoring installed prior to the demolition of the building next door.
